title: The quotient group acts on the fixed subscheme of a normal subgroup
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $G,Q$ be affine finite-type $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $i:N\hookrightarrow G$ be a closed normal subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], and let $q:G\to Q$ be a homomorphism representing the fppf quotient $G/N$ in the sense of [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure]: $q$ is flat, surjective and locally of finite presentation and $i$ identifies $N$ with its scheme-theoretic kernel. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, where separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $a:G\times_kX\to X$ be an action, meaning $a(1,x)=x$ and $a(g,a(g',x))=a(gg',x)$ as morphism identities. Products are scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $j:Y=X^N\hookrightarrow X$ be the closed subscheme representing universal $N$-fixed points supplied by [lem-sfb-universal-fixed-subscheme]: for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, $Y(A)$ consists of the $x\in X(A)$ for which $a_{A'}(i(n),x_{A'})=x_{A'}$ for every commutative $A$-algebra $A'$ and $n\in N(A')$. There exists a unique $k$-scheme action $b:Q\times_kY\to Y$ satisfying
$$j\circ b\circ(q\times\mathrm{id}_Y)=a\circ(\mathrm{id}_G\times j).$$
No smoothness or reducedness assumption on $G,N,Q,X$ is imposed, and $X$ need not be proper.

source.place: Theorem 7.1, printed pp.138–139, and the normal-series induction in Theorem 16.51, printed p.343. The quotient-action step implicit there is expanded by representable descent: Stacks Tag 023Q, descent.tex, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms.

proof.text: First record the covers needed for descent. The given flat, surjective, locally finitely presented map $q$ is a singleton fppf covering by [def-pc-fppf-site]. Every base change of it is fppf by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change]. Such a covering is fpqc: for each affine open $V$ in its target, base change to $V$ and apply [lem-pc-fppf-affine-refinement]; its finitely many affine opens in the source have images covering $V$, exactly the second condition of [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], while flatness is already part of fppf. In particular $p=q\times\mathrm{id}_Y:G\times_kY\to Q\times_kY$ is fpqc. So are $q\times\mathrm{id}_{Q\times Y}$ and $\mathrm{id}_G\times q\times\mathrm{id}_Y$, used successively to check associativity.

source.place: Tags 021M (definition-fppf-covering), 021O (lemma-fppf), 021P (lemma-fppf-affine); the finite-affine refinement verifies the definition of fpqc, as in Tag 022C (lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf-fpqc).

proof.text:
Put $c=a\circ(\mathrm{id}_G\times j):G\times_kY\to X$. For every $k$-algebra $A$, $g\in G(A)$, $y\in Y(A)$, every $A$-algebra $A'$ and $n\in N(A')$, normality [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] gives $g_{A'}^{-1}i(n)g_{A'}\in i(N(A'))$. Thus the action identities and universal fixedness give
$$i(n)\cdot(g_{A'}\cdot j(y_{A'}))=g_{A'}\cdot((g_{A'}^{-1}i(n)g_{A'})\cdot j(y_{A'}))=g_{A'}\cdot j(y_{A'}).$$
These are morphism identities: restrict the domain $N\times G\times Y$ to any affine open and take its tautological $A$-point; equality on these opens implies equality by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Apply the final, arbitrary-test-scheme factorization clause of [lem-sfb-universal-fixed-subscheme] to $W=G\times Y$ and $u=c$, for the restricted $N$-action on $X$. It yields a morphism $\alpha:G\times Y\to Y$ with $j\alpha=c$. The factorization is unique: $j$ is injective on all algebra-valued points by the same node, hence equality after $j$ implies equality on affine charts and then globally by gluing.

source.place: Theorem 7.1, printed pp.138–139, applied to the N-action; conjugation calculation expanding the normal-series argument of Theorem 16.51, printed p.343.

proof.text: The same injectivity after $j$ shows $\alpha(1,y)=y$ and $\alpha(g,\alpha(h,y))=\alpha(gh,y)$: after $j$ these are precisely the given action identities for $a$. It also shows $\alpha(i(n),y)=y$, since [lem-sfb-universal-fixed-subscheme] says the restricted $N$-action on $Y$ is the projection. All formulas are identities of morphisms, with the affine-chart test justified as in step 2 by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing].

source.place: Chapter 7(a) action identities and Theorem 7.1, pp.138–139.

proof.text:
Consider the two pullbacks of $\alpha$ to
$$R=(G\times Y)\times_{Q\times Y}(G\times Y).$$
An $A$-point consists of $(g_1,g_2,y)$ with $q(g_1)=q(g_2)$. Therefore $q(g_2^{-1}g_1)=1$. The given scheme-theoretic kernel property yields a unique $n\in N(A)$ with $g_1=g_2i(n)$, even when $A$ is nonreduced. Step 3 gives
$$\alpha(g_1,y)=\alpha(g_2i(n),y)=\alpha(g_2,\alpha(i(n),y))=\alpha(g_2,y).$$
Testing on each affine open of $R$ and applying [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] proves the required equality of morphisms on $R$. No surjectivity of $G(A)\to Q(A)$ has been used.

source.place: Tag 023Q, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms: verification of its overlap condition for the quotient kernel pair.

proof.text: The fpqc cover $p$ of step 1 and overlap identity of step 4 satisfy exactly the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], with target scheme $Y$. We obtain a unique scheme morphism $b:Q\times Y\to Y$ with $bp=\alpha$. It is over $k$: its two candidate structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ agree after $p$, and uniqueness in that same descent statement makes them equal. Composing $bp=\alpha$ with $j$ gives the required displayed equation.

source.place: Tag 023Q, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms, statement and first paragraph of proof, lines 4130–4154.

proof.text: Since $q$ preserves the identity, $b(1,y)=\alpha(1,y)=y$. For associativity, compare $b(u,b(v,y))$ and $b(uv,y)$ on $Q\times Q\times Y$. Pull back first by $q\times\mathrm{id}_{Q\times Y}$ and then by $\mathrm{id}_G\times q\times\mathrm{id}_Y$, the two covers of step 1. On $G\times G\times Y$ the two maps are $\alpha(g,\alpha(h,y))$ and $\alpha(gh,y)$, equal by step 3 and $q(gh)=q(g)q(h)$. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] twice gives equality before either pullback. Thus $b$ is an action. For any other candidate $b'$, the required equation gives $j b'p=j\alpha$. The injectivity of $j$ established in step 2 gives $b'p=\alpha$, so uniqueness in the descent statement gives $b'=b$.

source.place: Tag 023Q, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms: uniqueness, applied to the two successive base-change covers and then to p.

Sources checked: Milne iAG Theorem 7.1 (pp.138–139: fixed functor over all R-algebras R', closed subscheme for separated X), Milne Theorem 16.51 (p.343: normal-series induction, which uses the quotient action only implicitly, so proof_origin=agent is right) and Stacks 023Q descent.tex lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms. Step 1: q is fppf and so is its base change p (lem-trf). fppf implies fpqc because the affine refinement over each affine V gives affine opens of T_i whose images cover V (Stacks 022C); the two associativity covers are also base changes of q. Step 2: normality over every k-algebra gives the conjugation identity. Tested on tautological points and glued, it gives exactly the hypothesis of the arbitrary-W factorization clause of lem-sfb-universal-fixed-subscheme, applied to N, which is separated and of finite type as a closed subgroup of affine G. Uniqueness holds because j is injective on points. Step 3: α's action laws and N-triviality, by cancelling j. Step 4: the kernel pair uses the scheme-theoretic kernel over arbitrary A, with no surjectivity of G(A)→Q(A). Step 5: singleton fpqc descent gives b; k-linearity follows from uniqueness. Step 6: unit, associativity by descent uniqueness applied twice, and uniqueness of b by cancelling j and then p. Edge cases N=1, N=G, empty X and infinitesimal α_p all work, and no smoothness or reducedness is used. Route: lem-pc-fppf-affine-refinement is accepted as a declared generic tool; the other off-unit citations are definitions or Mathlib leaves. No SGA source is cited.
